notes:
Gate pass on the fake backend: G1-G9 pass with no finding and no warning (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null. No hardware was attached, native.py was never imported, the external pslab SDK and a PSLab serial device were never installed or opened, and no measurement was taken on a device.

NOT COVERED: the raw waveform returned by TCD1304.read_signal (3694 integration elements x 2 samples per element = 7388 samples, TCD1304.py:79-82). The upstream returns only that raw CH1 array and applies no wavelength calibration (TCD1304.py:75-87), so the driver reduces one capture to its largest sample (a scalar intensity) and exposes the integration time; the array itself never crosses the MHS boundary. cap.measure.spectrum.v1 is not bound because its required wavelength_min/wavelength_max inputs cannot be applied and no pixel-to-wavelength map is stated in the clone (the README's calibration is a manual CFL procedure, README.md:46-55). The fake returns 8 placeholder samples instead of 7388; that is test data, not a measurement.

The package's scalar functions: the read-only state integration_time (converted from the upstream seconds to ms) and master_clock_frequency (Hz); cap.measure.intensity.v1 (class verb read) with an optional one-shot integration_ms; and one write, integration_time via cap.device.configure.v1 (unit ms, native_unit s). The setter and the read action's one-shot input call the native _start_sh_clock after changing integration_time, as the constructor does (TCD1304.py:45-48, 72-73), so the SH clock follows the new value. The configure class floor is R1, so the device risk is R1, above the card floor R0; no class is widened.

Limits: both integration_ms inputs (the read action's optional input and the writable state integration_time) are Limit.operator_required. No text file of the clone states an integration time range; the constructor default 10e-6 s (TCD1304.py:35) is a default of the class, not a bound of the device. Until an operator supplies site-limits.json, every call that sets the integration time is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. site-limits.example.json is an example overlay (0.001 to 1 ms) and not a statement about any unit; fixtures/conformance.json carries test inputs (not device facts). The driver never clamps or invents a value.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's decision is direct-driver and is followed; the card's helper field names PythonObjectDriver, but the package is a decorated direct Driver. A config-only family table cannot express the native read_signal capture that returns an array and is reduced to a scalar, nor the constructor's power/clock startup. The direct Driver is the card's decision; no SerialDriver/ScpiDriver command table is involved.

Safety: the e-stop is the native poweroff (PV1 = 0, TCD1304.py:54-56) and the declared safe state is the CCD powered off; the @reset recovery calls poweron (PV1 = 5). This is a software stop, not a safety-rated channel; no independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, the device is R1, and no estop_physical_ref or SAFE-045 claim is made. G6 exercised the e-stop on the fake and an agent reset was refused on the hardware view.

Hardware path: native.py is a factory over the clone root module TCD1304 and the external pslab SerialHandler (TCD1304.py:15-18, 38). The clone has no setup.py, pyproject.toml or requirements.txt; .travis.yml lists Python 3.5 to 3.8 and names absent requirements.txt/Makefile. The hardware path was never run and is a human decision; the gate ran the fake backend only.

Test data: fake.py's start integration time 10e-6 s, master clock 2e6 Hz and 8 samples (peak 90.0) are placeholders marked # placeholder; test_driver.py mirrors them as test data. check-report.json is regenerated by the gate and is not part of the package. No extension id was used, so no catalogue_requests entry is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): SAFE-042 correction; still PASS. The @reset hook called poweron() (PowerSupply.pv1 = 5), so a safety reset re-energised the CCD supply that the e-stop turns off, which SAFE-042 forbids and the review of 2026-10-30 missed. The hook is removed: a reset only releases the latch and the supply stays off. poweron (TCD1304.py:50-52, documented as turning the TCD1304 on) is now the declared re-enable x-cap.opntec.power_on.v1 (reenable=True, CORE-086; MHS/changes/RE-ENABLE-AND-TERMINAL-STOP.md): refused while latched, no input, named in the reset receipt; TSAFE-001 sends it after the reset and before its recovery capture. The Safety sentence above about the @reset recovery, and the sentence that no extension id is used, are superseded; the new extension is listed in catalogue_requests. One Fact added; facts.md also corrects the device risk it stated (R1, the class floor of cap.device.configure.v1, not R0). Four package cases added, 7 pass. G1-G9 pass with no finding. The gate digest is unchanged: it identifies the gate's findings (none before or after), not the package content. Changed driver.py, facts.md, test_driver.py, reference.json, REFERENCE.md, RESULT.json, check-report.json. Source pin, DeepSeek authorship and driver.lock.json unchanged. No PSLab, hardware or human review.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class switches a detector's supply on: cap.optics.set_power.v1 sets the emitted power of a light source, not the 5 V supply of a CCD. The extension is the declared re-enable after a safety reset (CORE-086), takes no input and returns whether poweron() returned.
catalogue_requests.summary: Power the TCD1304 CCD on again (PowerSupply.pv1 = 5) after a safety reset.
